title: Rehang a wall-mount enclosure door on its two removable-pin hinges
instruction: Pick up the orange-headed hinge pins and push them fully down through both hinges of the grey enclosure door, then close the door and let go.
context: Enclosure doors on removable-pin hinges are hung by lining the door knuckles up between the frame knuckles and dropping the pins through. The body is modelled on the nVent Hoffman INLINE LHC252015 (250 x 200 x 150 mm, 16 gauge steel; datasheet: "Hinged door with removable hinge pins and self-grounding quarter-turn latch system", "Door opens 180 degrees"; Hoffman catalog pages 6.10-6.11). Loose stainless hinge pins are a catalogue item for Hammond Eclipse enclosures (part no. EPINSS, Hammond Electrical Products Guide pages 287-288). No maker publishes knuckle or pin dimensions, so the hinge is a representative 3-knuckle loose-pin hinge, our assumption to verify on a first build: fixed knuckles 10 mm OD x 15 mm with a 16 mm gap, a 14.5 mm door knuckle (0.75 mm axial play per side), 5.1 mm bores, 4.8 mm stainless pin.
setup: Station table; coordinates in mm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y left, heights above the table top. Plywood backboard 500 x 400 x 18 mm, vertical, front face at x 457. Grey powder-coated steel enclosure body 250 tall x 200 wide x 150 deep (LHC252015 outer size), 1.5 mm (16 gauge) walls with plain front edges (no flange trough, no gasket, not modelled), open toward the robot, back against the backboard, sitting on a 145 x 200 x 15 mm plywood spacer (body bottom 15 mm high), front face at x 307, spanning y -130 to +70; a white painted steel back panel (226 x 176 x 3 mm), a zinc DIN rail (160 x 35 x 7.4 mm) and 8 black plastic terminal blocks (6 x 38 x 55 mm) inside (visual only, no collision). Hinges: two representative machined zinc-plated steel 3-knuckle removable-pin hinges (our assumed geometry, drawings in cad/) on its left side wall, axis at x 300, y 75, centres 55 and 225 mm high; each has two fixed knuckles (10 mm OD, 15 mm long, 5.1 mm bore, 16 mm gap between them) on a 1.5 mm steel leaf, 23.6 mm long (spans x 303.0 to 326.6 mm), one strap alongside each knuckle, screwed to the side wall. Grey 16 gauge steel door 250 x 200 mm (1.52 mm nominal; the simulated plate collider is 1.6 mm) with 12 mm inward return flanges (side flanges inset 4.5 mm, top flange inset 7.5 mm, bottom flange flush), black molded-plastic quarter-turn wing knob (20 x 12 x 30 mm) 25 mm from the latch edge, one door knuckle (10 mm OD, 14.5 mm long, 5.1 mm bore) on a 1.5 mm steel door leaf 24 mm wide per hinge, on the outer face of the door plate, 0.78 kg; its hinge-side plate edge is 6.6 mm from the hinge axis, so at coaxial it is 13.2 mm short of the side wall's front edge; the hinge axis is 6.6 mm outboard of that edge. Door knuckle centres are 35.5 and 205.5 mm from the door bottom (44.5 mm from the top) on the leaves (drawings in cad/); the door hangs 4.5 mm above the body bottom with its knuckles centred in the gaps (3.75 mm once it rests on the lower knuckles). It stands upright, opened 90 degrees (latch edge toward the robot), hinge axis 40 mm in front of its hung position (x 260), its bottom 17 mm above the table, on a white acetal (POM) support block (17 mm tall, 63 mm wide, x 38.4 to 288, y 30 to 93) whose top is 2.5 mm below the height that puts the door knuckles in the gaps (19.5 mm); the block is disclosed, like an installer's shim or bench support, deliberately below hinge height, and is not an alignment stop. Two blue acetal (POM) guide strips (16 mm long, 20 mm wide, 30 mm tall, x 41.4 to 57.4) at the door's latch end: the outer strip (y 71.5 to 91.5) is 1.5 mm from the plate's outer face (y 70), the inner strip (y 34.9 to 54.9) is 13.5 mm from the plate's inner face (y 68.4). Nothing stops the slide: the right hand slides the door along the block to 12 mm short of the hinge axis, lifts it by about 1.75 to 3.25 mm off the block so the 14.5 mm knuckles fit the 16 mm gaps, and slides it the last 12 mm until its knuckles sit in line between the fixed knuckles (seen from above), and the ball tip gathers small offsets; a larger offset leaves the pin resting on the door knuckle until the door is moved into line. The skill tested is lifting and aligning the door, steadying it while the other hand drops the pins, then closing it. Two hinge pins (4.8 mm x 52 mm stainless shank, rounded tip, steel head 9 mm x 6 mm press-fit on the shank under an orange vinyl cap (generic 11 mm vinyl tube cap, 9 mm bore) 11 mm OD x 14 mm tall, 12 g) stand head up in a blue closed-cell EVA/PE foam pin block (60 x 75 x 40 mm, 6 x 6 mm holes 30 mm deep at x 220, y 195 and 225). Layout as in the setup image.
scoring: A hinge is pinned when a pin passes through all three of its knuckles: head underside from 0.5 mm below to 1 mm above the top knuckle face, pin within 3 deg of vertical and the pin head within 1 mm of the hinge axis and the pin tip within 3.7 mm of it (1 mm + 52 mm x sin 3 deg), tip at least 3 mm below the bottom knuckle, and the door's own knuckle on that pin (centre within 1 mm of the axis, wholly between the two fixed knuckles with no overlap over 0.5 mm with either, door within 5 deg of upright). 0.25: one hinge pinned. 0.5: both. 0.75: both, and the door closed (inner face from 1.5 mm into the enclosure front to 3 mm clear of it, at the top and bottom of the latch edge). 1.0: 0.75, door clear of the bench (2 mm), support block and guide strips, and both grippers open (at least 40 mm) and at least 50 mm from the door and pins for 1 s (20 steps). Score is the final state. 0 for the rest of the trial (latched) if: the door tilts more than 45 deg from upright; the door origin goes more than 50 mm below the table top or outside the table area (|x - 0.36| > 0.55 m or |y| > 0.65 m); or a pin head goes more than 30 mm below the table top or outside that area.
reset_notes: Stand the door back on the acetal support block between the guide strips at 90 degrees open and the two pins back in the pin block holes, head up.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX bodies, no hinge joint, 16-sided bores. Hinge geometry is a representative assumption (no published knuckle dimensions). No flange trough or gasket. Pair frictions: door on acetal 0.39, door on enclosure 0.6, pin in knuckles 0.4 to 0.5. Demo carry pose is pre-compensated for arm sag and wrist tilt under the door load (open-loop tuning). Latch fixed, not scored. Hardware not yet built or tested. No teleports, glue, injected forces, filters or state machines.
